sources.title: Sunscreen and sun safety
sources.notes: Manually checked public guidance. This small packet is not a complete clinical literature review.

claims.text: NHS guidance combines shade, protective clothing and sunscreen; sunscreen alone is not the whole strategy.
For sunscreen selection, NHS guidance specifies SPF 30 or higher and at least four-star UVA protection.
NHS guidance says sunscreen needs frequent reapplication, including after swimming, sweating or towel drying.

constraints: No attractiveness scores, shame, diagnosis, treatment or personalized medical advice.
No promise that grooming changes social status or guarantees appearance results.
Use only the approved claim IDs. A qualified editor must check suitability before publication.

draft.title: Sun Safety for Men: Practical Steps Beyond the SPF Number
draft.angle: This editorial explores how adult men can prioritize skin health through shade, clothing, and proper sunscreen application without focusing on aesthetic outcomes. It emphasizes that protection is a multi-layered strategy rather than relying solely on product selection.
questions: How can men integrate sun safety into their daily routine without it feeling like a chore?
What are the specific criteria for choosing an effective sunscreen that meets NHS standards?
Why is reapplication frequency often overlooked and how does it impact overall protection?

claim_checks.reason: Text accurately reflects NHS guidance on multi-layered sun protection.
Text correctly cites NHS SPF 30+ and four-star UVA requirements.
Text accurately states NHS reapplication guidelines for swimming and sweating.

review.reason: All claims are fully supported by the source packet; title and angle avoid unsupported promises or health advice.
